{{Short description|American mathematics educator}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=July 2021}}
'''Nadine S. Bezuk''' is an American mathematics educator, and a [[professor emerita]] of teacher education at [[San Diego State University]],{{r|em}} where she is a former associate dean and former Qualcomm Professor of Teacher Education,{{r|crmse}} the former director of the San Diego State University School of Teacher Education,{{r|ii}} and the former president and executive director of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators.

==Education and career==
Bezuk is originally from [[Pittsburgh]].{{r|ii}} She has a bachelor's degree in child development and early childhood education from the [[University of Pittsburgh]], and a master's degree and Ph.D. in mathematics education from the [[University of Minnesota]].{{r|cv}}

She worked as a K-12 mathematics teacher from 1981 through 1984, and joined the San Diego State University faculty in 1987.{{r|cv}}

She was president of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators from 1997 to 1999, and executive director from 2001 to 2014,{{r|cv}} and has also served as a director of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]].{{r|ii}}

==Book==
Bezuk coauthored the book ''Learning Mathematics In Elementary And Middle School: A Learner-Centered Approach'' (with [[Yvonne Pothier]], W. George Cathcart, and James H. Vance, Pearson, 2003; 6th ed., 2015).
